review.notes:
First-pass research, 2026-10-04, Codex: read the exact local questionnaire; used 2026 constitutional translation and original institutional analysis, KCNA’s March appointment account, Freedom House context, HRW reporting, OHCHR methodology and paragraphs 9–24, original device-law and software investigations, and the drug-law study abstract. Not all sources are independent for every claim: HRW repeats some OHCHR findings; constitutional translations are not treated as independent corroboration of each other. The UN report includes interviews and their access limitations. Historical drug provisions are not represented as a verified current consolidated code or used for current sentence lengths. No scores imported. A distinct review of these entries remains pending; no full sign-off. Distinct two-axis review, 2026-10-04, Codex (same AI agent): reread all 32 exact statements, directions, rationales and relevant passages. Corrected Democracy 04 from Agree to Disagree and 12 from Neutral to Agree after checking articles 93, 96 and 119–125: the questions specify the head of government, so the cabinet premier is the consistent referent. Kim’s head-of-state powers and immunity from recall cannot silently replace that office. These qualified answers do not assert competitive elections or independent legislative practice. Removed an unwarranted independence condition from the expert-panel rationale. Retained the suffrage mixed answer because formal education equality coexists with express disability exclusion. Reviewed surveillance and gathering inferences as support for the stated permissive powers, not proof of judicial independence. Kept duration-, context- and procedure-specific gaps unresolved. State announcements verify appointments, not democratic legitimacy; the 2024 legal study was read as an abstract, not its full paper. Reviewed the validation output by complete error categories: incomplete later axes, missing flag metadata and unfinished overall sign-off prevent archiving; no warnings or neighbours. No global review identity or date is entered because the 240-question assessment is unfinished. Cultural and immigration first pass, 2026-10-04, Codex: read all 32 exact local statements; added dated 2025–2026 enforcement and community records, consular entry/residence guidance, legal text and its provenance. Embassy sources are one publisher network, not independent corroboration of each other. The recovered law is unchecked OCR plus machine translation, so it is a qualified baseline cross-checked against consular guidance, not an official current consolidated English code. Remaining unknowns now specify the exact missing evidence. This is not full review sign-off. Distinct cultural/immigration review, 2026-10-04, Codex (same AI agent): reread each of the 32 exact statements and challenge the proposed inference separately from the research pass. Withdrew Immigration 02 because administrative permission requirements do not establish rejection of ordinary economic settlement. Applied that same distinction to job offers and graduation routes, which remain unknown. Retained Immigration 05 only as a qualified inference from positively specified political asylum categories, not proof of no asylum or a skills test. Immigration 06 rests on an explicit expulsion power and an earlier concrete announcement, not citizens’ emigration restrictions; King’s alleged motives are not treated as verified facts. Checked that Culture 04 is a substantive mixed response based on selective accommodation, not missing evidence. Culture 03/05/07/10/15 remain qualified inferences from explicit institutional mandates, with schools, public-language practice and international project funding distinguished from unsupported universal bans or budget percentages. Culture 09 remains unknown because attending a festival does not establish institutional scheduling. Confirmed that embassy reports belong to the same publisher network and that legal translation limitations are recorded. No complete-profile review sign-off, archive or publication is asserted. Military/international first pass, 2026-10-04, Codex: read all 32 exact statements; added nuclear-use law, September ministry statements, budget and conscription reporting, operative Russia treaty evidence, military-espionage research, current monetary implementation and human-rights responses. KCNA statements, their news reproductions and analyses are not independent witnesses to the same event. State allegations about adversaries are not adopted as verified facts. WithSecure research summary was read, not the linked full technical report. BTI’s 2026 label is distinguished from its older observation period. COP29 retrieval returned HTML instead of a PDF; the unread text is not cited as read evidence. No full sign-off.

Separate completion evidence challenge on 2026-10-05: read all current 240 question texts and compared the response rationales with their literal agreement directions. Corrected the initially mismatched first nine public/private rationales and signs before archival; bank order must not substitute for reading each question. Public/private-08 is qualified public-bank retention, not evidence of an implemented private-bank sector. Strong public ownership is not treated as high cash redistribution. Re-read the constitutional economy, local administration and rights provisions, BTI economic and welfare material, the UPR gender submission, UNICEF health programme and 2026 AI material. The constitutional translation is unofficial; BTI’s 2026 label covers an earlier observation period and is complemented by 2026 digital/assembly evidence. Statistical scarcity is disclosed, not filled by fictitious data. Every one of the 181 new responses is an educated assumption; strength reflects institutional evidence rather than claiming a documented exact questionnaire reply. Firearm law research improved authority-liberty-15 to -2 with historical-version limitations. All prior partial reviews are retained. No score target or neighbouring answer vector was used.

Contextual sources are attached to each. All neutral answers were individually challenged: formal suffrage exclusions, minority cultural continuity, military defensive purpose alongside foreign deployment, limited international cooperation, fiscal ambiguity, gender equality alongside sex-specific roles, mixed reproductive provision and coercion, sector-specific technology safeguards, and biological/environmental development interactions support conditional responses rather than automatic uncertainty. Culture-vs-Nature is not inferred from environmental policy, traditionalism or communist labels. Clinical developmental interventions and political pedagogy do not settle comparative genetic causation; all sixteen trait responses remain provisional.
